title: Naked Nouns
intro: Go to school. Have lunch. Love music. English drops the article completely for general statements, institutions and abstract nouns — the cases every rule-book skips past.

options: I go to school by bus.
I go to the school by bus.
I go to a school by bus.
A2.why: “Go to school” as a student: no article. It's the activity, not the building.

options: We have lunch at home.
We have lunch at the home.
We have the lunch at home.
A2.why: Meals take no article: “have lunch”. And “at home” never takes “the”.

options: She likes music.
She likes the music.
She likes a music.
A2.why: Music in general takes no article. Spanish says “la música”; English doesn't.

options: Dogs are loyal animals.
The dogs are loyal animals.
A dogs are loyal animals.
A2.why: General statements about a whole group use the plural with no article: “Dogs are…”.

options: He goes to bed at ten.
He goes to the bed at ten.
He goes to a bed at ten.
A2.why: “Go to bed” means go to sleep: no article.

options: I love chocolate.
I love the chocolate.
I love a chocolate.
A2.why: Things you like in general take no article: “I love chocolate”.

options: Water is essential for life.
The water is essential for the life.
A water is essential for life.
A2.why: Water and life in general: no article. Spanish uses “el agua”; English doesn't.

options: Children need love and support.
The children need the love and support.
Children need a love and support.
A2.why: Love and support in general are abstract nouns: no article.

options: We play football on Sundays.
We play the football on Sundays.
We play a football on Sundays.
A2.why: Sports take no article in English: “play football”, not “the football”.

options: I have breakfast at eight.
I have the breakfast at eight.
I have a breakfast at eight.
A2.why: Meals take no article: “have breakfast”, “have lunch”, “have dinner”.

options: My father goes to work by car.
My father goes to the work by car.
My father goes to work by the car.
A2.why: “Go to work” and “by car” are fixed phrases with no article.

options: Valencia is famous for oranges.
Valencia is famous for the oranges.
Valencia is famous for an oranges.
A2.why: Oranges in general: plural with no article, where Spanish would say “las naranjas”.

options: He was sent to prison for fraud.
He was sent to the prison for fraud.
He was sent to a prison for fraud.
B1.why: “Sent to prison” as a punishment: no article. It's the institution, not the building.

options: She's studying medicine at university.
She's studying the medicine at the university.
She's studying a medicine at university.
B1.why: Subjects and “at university” take no article in British English.

options: They travelled by train.
They travelled by the train.
They travelled by a train.
B1.why: Transport with “by” takes no article: “by train”, “by car”, “by bus”.

options: Information is power.
The information is the power.
An information is power.
B1.why: Information in general, as an idea: no article.

options: We need more information about the flight.
We need more an information about the flight.
We need more the information about the flight.
B1.why: “Information” is uncountable: never “an information”. “More information” needs nothing.

options: She gave me good advice.
She gave me a good advice.
She gave me the good advice.
B1.why: “Advice” is uncountable in English: no “a”, and never “advices”.

options: Furniture is expensive these days.
The furnitures are expensive these days.
A furniture is expensive these days.
B1.why: Furniture in general takes no article, and it's uncountable, so never “furnitures”.

options: He's afraid of spiders.
He's afraid of the spiders.
He's afraid of a spiders.
B1.why: Spiders in general: plural, no article. Spanish says “las arañas”.

options: Life isn't always fair.
The life isn't always fair.
A life isn't always fair.
B1.why: Life in general takes no article: “Life isn't always fair”.

options: Smoking is bad for your health.
The smoking is bad for the health.
A smoking is bad for your health.
B1.why: Smoking and health in general: no article. Spanish uses “el tabaco”, “la salud”.

options: Many people go to church at Easter.
Many people go to the church at the Easter.
Many people go to church at the Easter.
B1.why: “Go to church” to worship: no article. Festivals like Easter take none either.

options: In the Wild West, gold was worth a fortune.
In the Wild West, the gold was worth a fortune.
In the Wild West, a gold was worth a fortune.
B1.why: Gold as a material in general: no article.

options: He was taken to hospital after the crash.
He was taken to the hospital after crash.
He was taken to hospitals after the crash.
B2.why: British English: an injured person is “taken to hospital”. But a specific crash needs “the”.

options: My grandmother has been in hospital since Monday.
My grandmother has been in the hospital since the Monday.
My grandmother has been in a hospital since a Monday.
B2.why: In British English a patient is “in hospital”. Days like Monday take no article.

options: Crime has fallen sharply this year.
The crime has fallen sharply this year.
A crime has fallen sharply this year.
B2.why: Crime as a general problem: no article.

options: Unemployment rose last quarter.
The unemployment rose last quarter.
An unemployment rose last quarter.
B2.why: Unemployment as a general figure: no article, and it's uncountable.

options: She plays tennis every weekend.
She plays the tennis every weekend.
She plays a tennis every weekend.
Honesty is the best policy.
The honesty is the best policy.
An honesty is the best policy.
B2.why: Qualities like honesty take no article when you mean them in general.

options: He has luggage to check in.
He has a luggage to check in.
He has the luggages to check in.
Knowledge is valuable.
The knowledge is valuable.
A knowledge is valuable.
B2.why: Knowledge in general: no article, and it's uncountable.

options: They played chess by candlelight.
They played chess by the candlelight.
They played chess by a candlelight.
B2.why: “By candlelight” is a fixed phrase with no article, like “by moonlight”.

options: Before vaccines, smallpox killed millions.
Before the vaccines, the smallpox killed millions.
Before a vaccine, a smallpox killed millions.
B2.why: Vaccines in general and diseases like smallpox take no article.

options: The outlaw spent ten years in prison.
The outlaw spent ten years in the prison.
The outlaw spent the ten years in the prison.
B2.why: “In prison” as a prisoner: no article, just like “in hospital”.

options: Most Valencians have dinner quite late.
Most Valencians have the dinner quite late.
Most Valencians have a dinner quite late.
B2.why: Meals take no article: “have dinner”, just like “have lunch”.

options: Patience is a virtue.
The patience is a virtue.
A patience is a virtue.
C1.why: Patience as a general quality: no article, as in this old proverb.

options: Justice must be seen to be done.
The justice must be seen to be done.
A justice must be seen to be done.
C1.why: Justice as an abstract idea: no article.

options: Poverty remains a global challenge.
The poverty remains a global challenge.
A poverty remains a global challenge.
C1.why: Poverty as a general problem: no article.

options: Time heals all wounds.
The time heals all wounds.
A time heals all wounds.
C1.why: Time in general, as in this proverb, takes no article.

options: Theft is on the rise in big cities.
The theft is on the rise in big cities.
A theft is on the rise in big cities.
C1.why: Theft as a type of crime in general: no article.

options: Democracy depends on an informed public.
The democracy depends on an informed public.
The democracy depends on the informed public.
C1.why: Democracy as a system in general: no article.

options: The prisoners ate in silence.
The prisoners ate in the silence.
The prisoners ate in a silence.
C1.why: “In silence” is a fixed phrase with no article.

options: Research is the key to better treatments.
The research is the key to the better treatments.
A research is the key to better treatments.
C1.why: Research is uncountable: no “a”, and no “the” when you mean research in general.

options: Freedom of speech is a fundamental right.
The freedom of speech is a fundamental right.
A freedom of speech is a fundamental right.
C1.why: Freedoms and rights as general ideas take no article: “freedom of speech”.

options: Medicine changed more in the last century than in the previous thousand years.
The medicine changed more in the last century than in the previous thousand years.
A medicine changed more in the last century than in the previous thousand years.
C1.why: Medicine as a whole field: no article. “A medicine” would be one drug.

options: Nature always finds a way.
The nature always finds a way.
A nature always finds a way.
C1.why: Nature in general takes no article. Spanish says “la naturaleza”; English doesn't.

options: Progress in surgery owes a great deal to anaesthesia.
The progress in the surgery owes a great deal to the anaesthesia.
A progress in surgery owes a great deal to anaesthesia.
C1.why: Progress, surgery and anaesthesia in general: no articles. “Progress” is uncountable.
